Alex / Sean,

Quick update from runtime: we've ingested the traces you uploaded (thanks) and reproduced locally with a traffic replay. Short version: reproduced p99 spikes + intermittent 502s when client SDK performs aggressive ACK window coalescing and the streaming parser receives split trailer/header blocks across chunk boundaries.

Observations:
- The SDK variant Elysian is on (v2.3.1) batches outgoing frames and will sometimes coalesce an ACK/trailer into the preceding data frame. When the proxy/transport layer splits frames in the middle of the trailer, our streaming parser state machine can drop the trailing header block instead of buffering it. That results in the server treating the request as malformed and terminating the stream with a 502.
- Because many clients immediately retry, we see a burst of new requests that hit autoscaling and create contention; the interplay drives p99 to the 2-4s range as queuing increases.
- Replays show the parser's header accumulation buffer is sized for accumulating small splits but doesn't currently reconcile a split where a 'trailer' header arrives after the final data chunk boundary (edge case).

Short-term mitigation (can be rolled immediately):
1) Customer-side: Set REDWOOD_SDK_ACK_WINDOW=0 (env) or downgrade to v2.3.0 where coalescing is less aggressive. This reduces coalescing and avoids the split-trailer case.
2) Service-side: Enable lenient trailer parsing on the ingress proxy for legacy SDKs (accept and reassemble trailing headers across chunk boundaries). This is a fast server-side config flip.

We have a repro and a candidate hotfix in a branch that changes the parser to always buffer an extra 256 bytes at end-of-stream and treat incomplete trailer tokens as appendable; patch attached (sdk-hotfix.diff) along with ingest traces (ingest-trace-20260802.json.gz) and parser repro log.

I'll push the server-side lenient parsing flip now (low risk) and circulate a hotfix PR for the runtime. Will update in 20 minutes after the config flip.

—Soojin
